findings.title: DELETE without explicit LIMIT bound
findings.description: The normalized SQL omits an explicit LIMIT clause. The affected set is practically bounded only by the assumed primary-key uniqueness of COMPANY.ID; if that invariant ever changes, the predicate could delete multiple rows. Static observation; the primary-key assumption is unverified at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Add LIMIT 1 to the single-table DELETE, or verify COMPANY.ID as a primary key and pair it with an affected-row assertion of exactly one.

findings.title: State-guard race is silent without an affected-row check
findings.description: The COMPANY_STATE WHERE predicate is an optimistic concurrency guard. A concurrent state change between the caller's read and the delete yields zero affected rows, which is safe but silent unless the caller inspects the affected-row count.
findings.recommendation: Check the affected-row count after execution and surface a conflict to the caller when zero rows are deleted.

findings.title: Index and plan for the combined predicate unverified
findings.description: With safety_mode=connectivity-only and database_safety=unverified, index existence and the execution plan for the ID + COMPANY_STATE predicate could not be confirmed at runtime.
findings.recommendation: Confirm COMPANY.ID is the primary key in a privileged runtime check; add a composite index only if the filtered plan regresses.
